output.title: Where churn signals really start
output.body:
Churn signals usually do not start as a dashboard problem. They start with one owner noticing the same customers going quiet, buying less often, or sounding different when they do reach out.

For a 1–10 person business, the useful workflow decision is not “can we automate churn?” It is: do we already have a repeatable trail before a customer stops repeating, and who is looking at it? That is the line between gut feel and a pattern you can test.

AI only helps on the second part. If the evidence is already in email, CRM notes, order history, or support messages, the first step can still be manual: review one month of cancellations or lapses and list the last visible touchpoints, complaints, delays, or silence beforehand. If that trail does not exist, there is nothing tidy for a model to rescue.

That gives you a bounded pilot scope without pretending the software should make the decision. The owner still makes the call; the system just helps surface the pattern.
